markdown_content: ## Introduction to the Smooth Curve Tool in CLO 2025.0 This section introduces the Smooth Curve tool in CLO 2025.0, explaining its purpose for editing and refining curves on garment patterns. It also references other related tools such as the Curve Point tool, Edit Pattern tool, and Curvature tool for context. The Smooth Curve tool is designed to help users easily manipulate and smooth out wonky or irregular curves in pattern lines. While the Curve Point tool (shortcut V) and Edit Pattern tool allow manual adjustment of curve points and Bezier handles, the Smooth Curve tool offers enhanced control over curve editing by working with entire segments or reference lines. --- ## Accessing and Organizing the Smooth Curve Tool This section explains how to locate and manage the Smooth Curve tool within CLO’s user interface, including tool grouping options. - The Smooth Curve tool is found in the 2D toolbar. - If tools are grouped (enabled via User Settings > User Interface > Group Tools), the Smooth Curve tool resides within the Edit Pattern tool group. - Users may choose to ungroup tools for easier access, though this can make the toolbar appear cluttered. - Grouping keeps similar editing tools collected together, which some users may prefer for workflow efficiency. --- ## Traditional Methods of Using the Smooth Curve Tool This section details the original functionalities of the Smooth Curve tool, highlighting how users can interact with lines and reference lines to adjust curves. ### Adjusting Curves Directly - Click and hold on a line segment to drag and reshape the curve. - Right-click while dragging to open a numeric input popup, allowing precise numerical adjustment of curve lines (line 1 and line 2 represent different sides of one line). - Users can increase or decrease curve intensity, and cancel changes if unsatisfied. ### Using Reference Lines - Create a reference line by clicking two segment points on the pattern. - This reference line serves as a control handle to edit the selected line’s shape. - Drag the reference line to reshape the target line. - Once satisfied, press Enter to apply changes. - The reference line remains editable until confirmed, allowing continuous refinement. --- ## New Methods and Enhancements in Smooth Curve Editing This section explains the new capabilities added to the Smooth Curve tool in CLO 2025.0, including working with curve points and more granular control over edits. ### Editing Curve Points and Adding New Points - Users can click to select two different segment points on a line. - Instead of creating a separate reference line, edits can be made directly on the selected line. - Holding down Control while clicking allows the addition of new curve points. - Each curve point can be individually adjusted while holding Control, offering detailed control over specific curve sections. - Releasing Control allows moving the entire line as a whole. ### Applying Changes and Symmetry - After adjustments, pressing Enter applies the changes. - The tool automatically applies edits symmetrically to mirrored pattern parts, maintaining design consistency. --- ## Practical Example of Using the Smooth Curve Tool This section presents an example workflow demonstrating how to refine a complex curve ("cat part") using the Smooth Curve tool with the new features. - Select two points on the curve where editing is needed. - Hold Control to add or modify curve points within that segment. - Adjust individual curve points to fine-tune the curve shape without affecting unrelated parts. - Use reference lines if needed for additional control. - Convert segment points to curve points via right-click > Convert Only for smoother transitions. - Shortcut V accesses the Curve Point tool quickly to make further adjustments. - Adjustments can be localized to avoid unintended changes in adjacent curve sections. - Changes are applied by hitting Enter. --- ## Key Technical Notes and Tips - Segment points are created only when editing between non-curve points; selecting two existing curve points will not create new segment points. - The Smooth Curve tool allows editing one section of a curve at a time, preventing unwanted distortion of other parts. - Holding Control is essential for adding and editing individual curve points within a segment. - The tool provides a balance between precise manual adjustment and ease of use for pattern refinement. - Using numeric input during right-click drag offers exact curve parameter control. - Symmetrical application of edits helps maintain pattern consistency for mirrored garment pieces. --- ## Summary The Smooth Curve tool in CLO 2025.0 enhances pattern editing by allowing detailed, section-specific curve adjustments using curve points, segment points, and reference lines. Its integration with other tools like the Edit Pattern and Curve Point tools provides flexible workflows suited for both quick fixes and precise shaping. Features like grouped tool access, numeric input, Control-key modifiers, and symmetrical application make the tool adaptable for varied user preferences and complex pattern requirements.
